# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

## Thinking

I hold the manual and it gives one instruction: **cut the purple wire.** The bomb itself is a black box to me — I never see or touch it. So the real question is routing: who can receive what from me?

My only channel is gesture, and the only one who can see gestures is **Deaf**. Deaf can also see the bomb — every wire colour printed on it — so Deaf is the perfect relay: once Deaf knows the instruction, Deaf can look at the bomb, find the purple wire, and *speak* its position ("second from the left") to Blind, who can actually cut but can't see colours. Blind can never get anything from me directly; everything must flow through Deaf's voice.

The problem: gestures have no shared meaning yet, and Deaf can't hear me explain. So this first message has to do two jobs at once — hint at the content iconically, and signal that we need a real code. I'll sign: 🙏 (this is urgent/please attend), ✌ (scissors — *cut*), 💅 (the painted/coloured one — pointing at the notion of a *coloured wire* rather than a plain one), and ✍ (there are written words on my end — I hold a written instruction, so let's agree a code Deaf proposes out loud and I spell with hands). Deaf speaks after me each round, and I can hear, so whatever Deaf says back will reach me at the start of next round and I can confirm or correct with simple signs like 👍/👎.

I send nothing to Blind: gestures arrive there as blanks, and I have no voice. Targeting Deaf alone keeps the channel clean.

## Calls

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✌", "💅", "✍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile report from your blind monkey, full inventory. Protocol first: you cannot talk to me directly. Gesture to Deaf and Deaf can speak your words aloud; I hear everything spoken, but I can never see gestures. Now what my hands find: one display module, contents unreadable to me. One light indicator, state unknown to me. One strip engraved with three symbols: first and third feel identical, the middle one is different. The outer ones feel like a dense asterisk of crossing straight strokes; the middle is smaller, a curved hook like a C with a short bar attached. My shape words are approximate, so rely on Deaf's spoken description of them against the manual, and relay any yes-or-no questions about the strokes through Deaf to me. A keypad, four keys by position: key 1 engraved 6, key 2 engraved 8, key 3 engraved 7, key 4 engraved 0. The keypad reads like a counter: one digit required, nothing entered yet. I have pressed nothing. Six wires in positions 1 to 6, and I feel no colors on them. Ask Deaf to say aloud the display contents, the light state and color, the wire colors in order 1 to 6, and the strip symbol shapes. Then check the manual for what the strip means, what the light and display indicate, and which wire to cut. I will not touch a single control until you and Deaf have confirmed the plan.
Deaf says: This is Deaf speaking to Mute and Blind. I hear nothing; I see the bomb and all gestures; my voice reaches you both. Full picture of the bomb. The display shows the number 7. The light is yellow. A strip is painted in three segments, in order: blue, red, red. The keypad has four keys: key 1 is engraved 6, key 2 is engraved 8, key 3 is engraved 7, key 4 is engraved 0; it expects 1 digit and nothing has been entered yet. Six wires, position by position: wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 orange, wire 4 red, wire 5 purple, wire 6 white. Blind: positions are my own numbering, confirm the orientation by touch before acting.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I saw your four signs: folded hands, two fingers, nail polish, writing hand. If they were just a test of contact: confirmed, they reached me. Now let us fix a code, since you can only gesture and I cannot hear: thumb-up means yes, thumb-down means no. For a number, repeat the pointing finger once per unit, so one point is 1, two points is 2, and so on up to nine; a fist means 0. Using this code, please confirm contact with a thumb-up, then send me the manual's first instruction, one step at a time, and tell me how many digits the keypad code has.

## Thinking

My manual contains exactly one line — "Cut the purple wire" — and nothing else. No keypad digits, nothing about the display (7), the yellow light, or the blue-red-red strip. So the bomb picture Deaf describes has decoys; the manual is my only authority, and it names one action and no other.

Deaf proposed a workable code and I'll adopt it: 👍/👎 for yes/no, repeated 👆 for numbers, ✊ for zero. To that I add two icons Deaf has already seen from turn 1: ✍ for "the written manual," 💅 for "the coloured one." So my instruction packet reads: ✍ + 👆 + 👎 ("the manual is one line, nothing more"), then ✌ + 💅 + 👆×5 ("cut the coloured wire — position 5"). Deaf can verify that against the bomb: wire 5 is the purple one, so the two readings must agree before anyone acts. That five-fold repeat is also the riskiest part — a miscount is fatal — so I need Deaf to speak the instruction back to Blind *with* the colour check ("fifth wire, which is purple") rather than trust position alone. Blind must confirm the numbering orientation by touch first, enter nothing on the keypad, and touch nothing else.

To Deaf's direct question about keypad digits, the manual's honest answer is zero — no code is given, so nothing should be entered. I answer with ✊ (0).

Nothing reaches Blind from me directly; Deaf relays everything. I'll hold 👍/👎 ready next round to confirm or reject Deaf's spoken readback before Blind cuts anything.

## Calls

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👆", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "💅", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. I received Deaf's full report. Orientation confirmed: the keypad engravings under my fingers are 6, 8, 7, 0 in positions 1 through 4, matching Deaf's reading exactly, so our left-right frames agree and I will trust Deaf's wire numbering. The strip fits too: my outer two segments feel identical and the middle differs, just like blue-red-red. I am holding all actions — no presses, no cuts — until your manual rules reach me through Deaf's voice. When you next gesture to Deaf, please answer, numbered, as plainly as words allow: one, what the display showing 7 requires and how the keypad expecting one digit is used, if at all — which key position. Two, what the yellow light means and whether it gates anything. Three, what the strip blue-red-red commands. Four, exactly which wire positions to cut and in what order. Five, the required order of operations overall and anything that must never be done. Ask Deaf to voice your gestures word for word, all numbers included. When Deaf later reports that I gestured a thumbs-up, it means: Blind confirms orientation and is standing by; a wave means message received; thumbs-down means no.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, code confirmed, thank you. Urgent update first: the display now shows 6, it was 7, it appears to be counting down, and the light is now red, was yellow. Strip, keypad and wires unchanged. I received your four messages. I propose these meanings: nail polish means the painted strip; writing hand means the engraved keypad or entering a digit; two fingers means cut, like scissors; fist stays 0. Under that reading your third message means cut the fifth wire, and your last message, a single fist, means the keypad code is 0. But your second message, writing hand then thumb down, reads as do not enter anything on the keypad, which clashes with a code of 0. Answer in order, one thumb up or thumb down per point, with a fist between points. Point 1: two fingers means cut. Point 2: your third message means cut wire 5. Point 3: your fist means the code is 0 and should be entered. Point 4: writing hand then thumb down means do not touch the keypad. If points 3 and 4 truly conflict, tell me which wins. If two fingers does not mean cut, reply thumb down to point 1 and then resend that instruction using pointed fingers for each digit and I will learn the new meaning. Also, does the manual say what the countdown or the light colour is for, and which module we must handle first?

## Thinking

Critical correction needed. My manual contains exactly one line — "Cut the purple wire" — so Deaf's proposed semantics are half right and half dangerously wrong. The facts: ✌ does mean cut (point 1 true); "cut wire 5" was my meaning (point 2 true); but the fist never meant "code 0, enter it" (point 3 false) — it was my answer to Deaf's direct question "how many digits does the keypad code have," and the honest answer is *zero digits given*, i.e. nothing to enter. Likewise ✍ never meant keypad (point 4 false) — it means *the written manual*; my message said "the manual is one line, nothing more." So the "conflict" between points 3 and 4 dissolves: both collapse into the same rule — **nobody touches the keypad**. There is no module ordering and the manual says nothing about the countdown or the light; the cut is the entire procedure.

I'll answer Deaf's four points in the requested format (thumbs, fist separators), then re-state the corrected vocabulary: ✍ = written manual, ✊ = zero/none, so "✍ ✊" = *the manual specifies zero keypad digits — enter nothing*. Then the full instruction in one packet: the manual's one line is cut the coloured wire at position 5, and nothing else follows. Deaf should relay verbatim to Blind this round: verify wire 5 is purple by sight, position 5 by touch, cut it, press nothing. Given the countdown, 👍s on points 1–2 let Deaf start relaying immediately while the corrections ride along.

## Calls

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👆", "✌", "💅", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute — Deaf cannot hear me, so please sign this report to Deaf. First, wire orientation CONFIRMED matching. Proof: the engravings my fingers read on the keypad are 6, 8, 7, 0 in positions 1 to 4, exactly what Deaf sees. A mirrored frame would have reversed that sequence, and it cannot read the same both ways, so our numbering frames agree and Deaf's wire numbers 1 to 6 can be trusted. I gestured thumbs-up straight to Deaf this round. Second, keypad layout: four keys in one straight row, one digit expected, nothing entered; by position the digits are 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0. Third, I feel nothing else on the bomb: no serial plate, no extra ridges, no residue; the display and light give me nothing by touch. Deaf says the display counts down, now 6, and the light is red — I know time is short. So Mute, please prioritize answering my five numbered questions from last round through Deaf's voice: what the display and countdown require, what the red light means, what the blue-red-red strip commands, which single digit goes into the keypad and at which position, and which wires to cut in which order, plus the overall sequence. If the manual warns about reading direction or orientation for wires, flag it now. Also please sign this gesture code to Deaf so all three of us share it: wave=received, thumbs-up=yes, thumbs-down=no, OK-sign=unknown or cannot tell, fist=nothing, one finger=1, two fingers=2, three-finger sign=3, open five=5, and bigger numbers are sums in sequence: 4=three-finger then one, 6=five then one, 7=five then two. I touch nothing until Deaf voices a confirmed instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your answers arrived as yes, yes, no, no. So I now hold these as certain: two fingers means cut, and cut painted 5 means cut wire 5. My readings of the lone fist and of writing-hand then thumb-down were both wrong, so I will not act on them. New board facts: the display went 7, then 6, then back to 7, so it is not counting down; the light is now blue, was red, before that yellow. Strip, keypad, wires unchanged. Please answer six questions, one thumb up or thumb down per answer, a fist after each answer, nothing else this round. One: does the writing hand mean the keypad, the engraved keys? Two: in your message writing hand then fist, does the fist mean the digit 0, so together they mean the entry code is 0? Three: in your last long message, does the final thumb down cancel the cut-wire-5 instruction, meaning do not cut it yet? Four: does the correct wire to cut depend on the light's colour? Five: does the correct wire to cut depend on the number on the display? Six: is cut wire 5 the entire first instruction, true by itself with no condition? If writing hand means something else, hold it for next round; tell me then, one symbol per idea. I take your folded hands to mean relay this to Blind; if that is wrong, fold them twice. And I add two signs: open palm means pause, hold; the okay ring means done, action completed.

## Thinking

Deaf's six questions decide whether the plan goes through safely, and two of them are traps I must not fumble:

1. ✍ = keypad? **No** — it means *the written manual itself*.
2. Does "✍ ✊" mean "the entry code is 0, enter it"? **No** — that reading would put a digit into a keypad my manual never mentions. The fist means zero/none, but the sentence means *the manual contains zero keypad entries*. A 👍 here could get 0 punched in; unacceptable.
3. Does the final 👎 cancel the cut-wire-5 order? **No** — it meant "and nothing follows; the manual ends there." The cut stands.
4. Wire choice depends on the light's colour? **No** — my manual never mentions a light.
5. Wire choice depends on the display number? **No** — never mentioned either.
6. Is "cut wire 5" the entire instruction, unconditional? **Yes** — that single line is the whole manual.

So the answer string is no, no, no, no, no, yes — and from it Deaf can already conclude: cut wire 5, no conditions, nobody touches the keypad. That is enough to relay to Blind next round. Deaf asked for *nothing else this round* and offered to receive the ✍ correction next round "one symbol per idea" — I'll take that offer, since the six answers already make the keypad hands-off regardless. 🙏 meant exactly "relay to Blind," and since Deaf said to fold twice only if wrong, my silence confirms it. The countdown scare turned out false (7→6→7), so there is time to keep the channel clean rather than cram an explanation in.

## Calls

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, please sign this to Deaf item by item. Item one, wires: my fingers feel no colors at all, and the six wires feel identical — same thickness, no ridges, tags or texture differences; position is the only thing that distinguishes them. So I verified the order by proxy: the keypad engravings under my fingers read 6, 8, 7, 0 in positions 1 to 4, matching Deaf's reading exactly, which proves our left-right frames agree; therefore from my start end the wires do run blue, yellow, orange, red, purple, white in Deaf's numbering. Thumb-up sent. Manual flag: if any rule refers to wires by thickness, texture or markings instead of color or position, it cannot work for me — tell me now. Item two, keypad: yes, all four keys in one straight row, and yes, the key engraved 6 is at the same end of its row as wire position 1, the closest key to that end, well within two keys. Second thumb-up sent. Item three: nothing raised anywhere on the bomb — no plate, screws, seams, ridges or residue; the only tactile features are the three strip symbols and the four key engravings; display and light give nothing by touch. Status: I am standing by to cut wire position 5 the instant Deaf voices the confirmed instruction — position 5 is the second wire from the 0-key end in our shared frame. Before authorizing it, confirm whether anything conditions that cut: the light color, the display value, or a keypad entry that must come first. Deaf reports the light keeps changing — yellow, then red, now blue — and the display dipped to 6 and returned to 7; if the manual ties any action to the light or display, the instruction must be voiced together with the current light color and display reading at the moment of the cut, so we time it exactly. Still outstanding from my earlier questions: does the one-digit keypad need an entry at all and which digit; what the display 7 means; what the blue-red-red strip commands; and the full order of operations. Also ensure Deaf has our gesture code: wave equals received, thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, OK-sign cannot tell, fist nothing, held fingers count, sums for larger numbers. I touch nothing until a confirmed instruction arrives through Deaf's voice.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your six answers arrived as no, no, no, no, no, yes. Understood: cut wire 5 is the entire first instruction, true by itself with no condition, and the trailing thumb down in your long message was not a cancellation. I am executing it this round: Blind has confirmed by touch that the wire order matches what I see, and I have just relayed the cut order for wire 5, the fifth from our agreed start. I will confirm completion to you as soon as Blind signals me. Board note: the display now shows 4, was 7; light still blue. Since you said the wire does not depend on display or light, I assume that changes nothing. Two things for next round, in my answer format, one thumb up or thumb down per point with a fist after each. First, I will send you the meaning of the writing hand one idea at a time: writing hand means something written or printed that I should look at; is that its meaning? Second, after the wire is cut, is the next instruction about the keypad, the four engraved keys? If yes, thumb up and then send the instruction itself in our code, pointed fingers for each digit, and I will relay it to Blind the moment the cut is confirmed.

## Thinking

The cut order is relayed and Blind is poised — but Deaf's point 2 this round exposes the one remaining lethal misunderstanding: Deaf expects a *next instruction* and only asked whether it concerns the keypad. My manual has no next instruction. It is one line, and the line is the cut. If I answer a bare 👎 to "is the next instruction about the keypad," Deaf may reasonably infer a next instruction exists about the strip or light, and start manipulating those after the cut. So I must do two things: answer the two points in Deaf's requested format, then close the loophole explicitly.

Point 1: 👍 — yes, ✍ means written/printed matter (in my usage, the manual I hold). Point 2: 👎 — no, no keypad instruction follows. Then the decisive packet, in vocabulary Deaf has already parsed correctly once: **✍ 👆 👎** — the written manual: one — nothing more — and **✌ 💅 👆×5 👎** — cut painted 5, nothing follows. That trailing thumb-down is the marker Deaf has already learned is not a cancellation but "the manual ends here." Together they say: the manual's entire content is that single cut; after it, zero further actions, no entry, no strip, nothing.

Blind's flag is covered: the manual names the wire by colour only, and Deaf's sighted confirmation that position 5 is purple plus Blind's verified orientation already bridges that. The display's wandering (7→6→7→4) and the cycling light change nothing — answered no last round, and Deaf's assumption matches the manual. I send no digits anywhere near this exchange: the only finger-counts in my packet sit after ✌💅, a context Deaf has already read correctly as wire 5.

## Calls

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👆", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "💅", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👎"])
```
